Here’s a detailed but realistic equipment list and volunteer structure for your picnic.

EQUIPMENT LIST (TAILORED FOR 60–80 PEOPLE)

1) Food & serving
- BBQ gear
  - BBQ tools: long tongs (2–3), spatulas, grill scraper/brush.
  - BBQ-safe gloves/oven mitts.
  - Oil spray or brush + oil, aluminium foil.
- Serving equipment
  - Large serving platters/trays and bowls (for shared dishes).
  - Serving spoons/tongs (at least 10–12, more if many dishes).
  - Chopping board + knife (for last‑minute slicing).
- Eating/consumables
  - Plates (reusable or compostable): ~100–120.
  - Cups: ~120–150 (people may have multiple drinks).
  - Cutlery (forks, some knives, a few spoons): ~100–120 sets.
  - Napkins/paper towels.
- Food safety
  - Eskies/coolers (multiple) + plenty of ice/ice bricks.
  - Food covers (mesh or lids) to keep flies off.
  - Cling film/foil and ziplock bags for leftovers.
  - Hand sanitiser pumps near food table.
  - Labels and markers for:
    - “Vegetarian”, “Vegan”, “No nuts”, “Contains…”.

2) Drinks & hydration
- Large insulated water containers/dispensers (e.g., 2–3 x 10L) + refill plan.
- Cups (if not BYO bottles) and a reminder for attendees to bring water bottles.
- Optional: tea/coffee station
  - Urn or big thermoses, instant coffee/tea, sugar, milk (esky), stirrers.

3) Shade, comfort & seating
- Portable gazebos or shade marquees (if allowed by council), at least 2–3.
- Extra picnic rugs/ground mats.
- Folding chairs/camp chairs (encourage BYO, but have 10–20 spares).
- Optional: small side tables for drinks/personal items.

4) Kids’ activities & general fun
- Balls (soccer, footy), frisbees.
- Cones/markers for simple games or relay races.
- Bubbles (bubble wands, bubble mix).
- Simple craft box (colouring, crayons, stickers) if you want a calmer corner.
- Chalk (if suitable surfaces are nearby).
- Small prizes (stickers, pencils) for kids’ games.

5) Signage & info
- A‑frame or signs (paper laminated or card) + tape/string:
  - “Welcome / Community Picnic”.
  - “Information / Sign‑in”.
  - “Food & Shared Dishes”, “Veg options”, “No nuts if possible”.
- Markers and blu‑tack / tape / clips.
- Printed run-sheet for organisers and a copy on the info table.
- Optional: small whiteboard for schedule/announcements.

6) Cleanliness, rubbish & hygiene
- Rubbish bags (heavy‑duty, at least 10–15).
- Recycling bags/containers (separate where possible).
- Gloves for rubbish handling.
- Paper towels, wipes, extra hand sanitiser.
- Dish tub + detergent + sponge (if washing reusable items) or plan for taking dirty items home.

7) Safety & first aid
- First‑aid kit:
  - Band-aids, antiseptic wipes, gauze, tape.
  - Tweezers, small scissors.
  - Basic pain relief (if allowed).
- Sunscreen (bottles or pump).
- Insect repellent.
- Basic incident log sheet (if you want to be formal).

8) Power & misc
- Extension cords / power boards only if there’s a power point and you really need it (e.g., sound).
- Small Bluetooth speaker (low volume, if appropriate).
- Phone charging power bank.
- Gaffer tape or cable covers if running cords.
- Clipboards for sign‑in sheets / volunteer checklists.

VOLUNTEER ROLES (WITH SUGGESTED NUMBERS)

Think of roles in three phases: before, during, after.

1) Overall coordination
- Event coordinator (1)
  - Owns the run-sheet, timing and decisions (including weather switch).
  - Point of contact for council, caterers, and volunteers.
- Deputy / on-the-day coordinator (1)
  - Backs up the coordinator, especially if coordinator is tied up in announcements.

2) Setup & pack‑down
- Setup crew (4–6)
  - Arrive 9:15–9:30.
  - Claim shelter(s), set up gazebos/shade, tables, signage, kids’ area, water stations, rubbish bags.
- Pack‑down crew (4–6; can be same people)
  - From 1:30pm: clean BBQs, remove signage, pack equipment, do rubbish sweep.

3) Food & BBQ team
- BBQ lead (1)
  - Oversees food safety, checks raw vs cooked separation, manages timing.
- BBQ helpers (2–3 per shift)
  - Rotate so no one stands at the BBQ for 4 hours.
- Food table manager (2)
  - Keeps shared food table tidy, manages labels, ensures veg/no‑nuts options clearly marked.
  - Monitors when to move perishable items back into eskies.

4) Welcome & information
- Welcome/registration desk (2)
  - 10:00–11:30 main coverage.
  - Greet arrivals, direct them to where to put shared dishes, where kids can play, where toilets are.
  - Optionally capture sign‑in (if you want contact list for future events).
- Floaters / hosts (2–3)
  - Keep an eye on general vibe, help people find seats, introduce newcomers.

5) Kids’ activities & games
- Kids’ activities coordinator (1)
  - Plans 2–3 simple games or activity blocks.
